rootCauseHypothesis: Supplier SUP-EU-014 (Valencia Pectinas S.A.) declared force majeure on 2026-09-02 following a fire in the extraction hall of its Valencia plant. All open purchase orders for ING-PEC-450 are suspended with no confirmed restart date; the supplier indicates 10 to 14 weeks. ING-PEC-450 is a single-source critical ingredient with no inbound replenishment in transit, so the three consuming plants will run down existing stock at 310, 240 and 185 kg per day respectively. Depletion at PLANT-FR-01 in 12 days, PLANT-DE-02 in 15 days, PLANT-BE-01 in 18 days.
notes: Second material failure from this supplier in three years; see post-mortem PM-2024-014 for the 2024 precedent on the same ingredient. Group holds 17,700 kg of ING-PEC-450 at the two unaffected sites (11,500 kg at PLANT-ES-01, 6,200 kg at PLANT-FR-03) which is available for reallocation and represents roughly 24 additional days of group cover. 14 SKUs affected representing approximately EUR 6.1 million of weekly revenue. Qualified alternate SUP-EU-023 can supply within 21 days but only at 40,000 kg per month, about 55% of requirement, and at an 18% price premium.

rootCauseHypothesis: Monsoon disruption to Kerala road freight has extended SUP-APAC-002 outbound lead times from 42 to an observed 58 days across the last two shipments. Current stock and in-transit volume still cover more than a quarter, so this is a watch-list signal rather than an active incident.
notes: Qualified alternate SUP-NA-012 can cover the full requirement at a 12% premium with a 38-day lead time. No action required before 2026-10-15. Flagged here because SKU-YOG-006, SKU-YOG-007, SKU-YOG-008 and SKU-DES-004 also sit inside the pectin incident scope, so any reformulation work should account for both ingredients at once.

rootCauseHypothesis: Seasonal decline in raw milk fat content across the SUP-EU-031 collection area reduced cream yield by 6.2% against plan for three consecutive weeks. Cream has a 21-day shelf life and cannot be stockpiled, so the signal reflects a yield squeeze rather than a supply failure.
notes: Resolved on 2026-08-30 by increasing the SUP-EU-007 call-off from Leeuwarden at a EUR 0.19 per kg premium, total incremental cost EUR 34,000. Retained here as a closed reference case showing how a short-shelf-life dairy signal differs from a shelf-stable hydrocolloid signal: no reallocation was possible and the only lever was a second qualified source.
